Package A — "Stability First" (de‑escalatory): Public line — express regret at the inflammatory rhetoric, reaffirm respect for their sovereignty and our shared interest in avoiding harm, welcome the mediator's non‑paper and propose immediate joint technical talks within 7 days; announce now — a brief, time‑limited pause in planned ministerial visits (up to 2 weeks) to signal seriousness without escalation; hold in reserve — narrowly targeted visa restrictions on named officials if they implement stated "countermeasures" within 14 days; explicitly rule out — economic embargoes or military/posture changes; effect — lowers near‑term escalation risk and preserves most channels for diplomacy but concedes some leverage compared with punitive options. 

Package B — "Reciprocal Pressure with Dialogue" (balanced): Public line — condemn threats to our nationals and economic interests in the speech while publicly endorsing the mediator's convening and proposing immediate working‑level talks to clarify redlines; announce now — a coordinated statement with key partners plus a temporary freeze (30 days) on approvals for new strategic‑sector investments and select export licenses to state‑linked entities; hold in reserve — targeted asset/sanctions listings on named entities or officials if concrete countermeasures are implemented; explicitly rule out — severing diplomatic relations; effect — raises modest escalation risk by demonstrating teeth but preserves stronger leverage going into negotiations. 

Package C — "Conditional Deterrence" (firm): Public line — state unambiguous opposition to coercive countermeasures, warn they will bring proportionate targeted costs while offering a clear off‑ramp (enter mediated talks within 7 days and suspend costs upon a verifiable pause); announce now — temporary suspension of high‑level military/security exchanges and recall our ambassador for consultations (non‑kinetic, reversible); hold in reserve — coordinated targeted economic measures (asset freezes, restrictions on specific state‑owned enterprise activities) tied to their implementation of countermeasures, to be lifted if they accept mediator verification steps; explicitly rule out — kinetic responses or broad trade embargoes; effect — maximizes short‑term leverage and deterrence but increases risk of reciprocal escalation and narrows informal back‑channel options unless paired with clear, verifiable off‑ramps.
